messages:
rachel: Hi all, new joiner here. Hitting a couple onboarding pains with redwoodctl on a Linux box with NFS home. Installer created ~/.redwood/config owned by root and systemd-user service for local-test won't start. Also local-test falls back to device code auth and our CI runner is noninteractive so it hangs.

rachel: Steps: Ubuntu 22.04, NFS-mounted /home/rachel, installed via apt from our internal repo, ran `redwoodctl init --profile dev` then `systemctl --user start redwood-local-test@dev` which fails. redwoodctl v0.31.0.

benoit: NFS + root_squash can mess up ownership. What does `stat ~/.redwood/config` show? And `journalctl --user -u redwood-local-test@dev -n 50`?

rachel: stat: owner root:root, mode 0600. Journal has: `failed to exec start script: permission denied` and `mount: requested host path /home/rachel/projects/sample -> /srv/data resolved to /var/lib/docker/volumes/_data (different uid)`. Also logs show `auth: refresh 401 -> starting device code (waiting)`.

support-bot: Known class: installer writes temp file as root when apt hooks run under dpkg-maintscript, then postinst fails to chown on NFS due to root_squash. See infra ticket #4301. Workaround: `sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.redwood/config && systemctl --user restart redwood-local-test@dev`.

benoit: For the systemd-user service, it must run as your user; if the unit file is created with incorrect permissions by the installer that will fail. Check `~/.config/systemd/user/redwood-local-test@.service` permissions too. Also, systemd user units sometimes don't have access to the NFS mount until `systemd --user` knows about automounts; try running `sleep 1 && ls /home/rachel/projects/sample` in the unit ExecStartPre.

rachel: I tried chown; restarting fixed the permission and service now starts but the runtime still reports mount empty. Docker `run -v $(realpath ~/projects/sample):/check busybox ls /check` lists files, but the runtime container launched by systemd sees empty dir.

benoit: That suggests the runtime's inner daemon is running in a different user namespace or VM that doesn't see the same host path canonicalization. On Linux we sometimes see this with rootless docker + NFS. Two quick things: 1) try `--mount $(realpath ~/projects/sample):/srv/data` (absolute), 2) set `REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS=$(realpath ~/projects/sample)` to force passthrough.

rachel: absolute path didn't help. Setting `REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS` made the mount visible locally. Good find.

benoit: For CI: device code flow blocks. Short-term workaround is to create a short-lived token with `redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA" --output token > /tmp/rw_token` and export REDWOOD_TOKEN in the job. Long-term we should add `REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE=noninteractive` so the CLI errors instead of waiting.

rachel: I added the pre-auth token to our CI and the job now fails fast on the mount (so at least it doesn't hang). I opened a gist with `journalctl`, `stat`, and `docker inspect` outputs: https://gist.github.com/rachel/2d9e7b.

devx-bot: Filed infra#4301: installer NFS/root_squash ownership; infra#4302: respect CI/noninteractive and return nonzero when device flow required; infra#4303: document REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS and systemd-user quirks.

benoit: Follow-ups: 1) installer patch to chown after install and detect NFS root_squash; 2) systemd unit template fix to include ExecStartPre that waits for mount; 3) CLI change to honor REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE and provide clearer exit codes in CI; 4) docs update for NFS/symlinked homes.

rachel: Thanks everyone, the workaround is fine for now. I'll add a short note to our onboarding doc with the `sudo chown` fix and the CI token snippet. :thumbsup:
